messages:
alex: heads up — after yesterday's batching heuristic tweak I see KV-cache page-table churn on H100 runs. p99 gen latency spikes on longctx workloads (64k). looks correlated with increased evict churn and PT fragmentation.

morgan: can you paste the perf snapshot/logs?

alex: pasted run summary: evict_count/sec jumped from ~120 to ~460 after change; pt_frag_index metric x3; cache_resident_rate dropped from 0.87 -> 0.62 on the same workload. GPUs affected: H100 primarily, A100 shows milder but consistent token-thr drops.

alex: config diff that landed:
```
# old
batching:
  batch_threshold: 32
kernel_selection:
  prefer_small_batch_kernels: false
# new
batching:
  batch_threshold: 16
kernel_selection:
  prefer_small_batch_kernels: true
```

sasha: interesting — switching to the small-batch tiled kernel for seq<512 batch<16 looks like it touches pages in a different order. the tiled loop does an inner prefetch that ends up touching many PT entries (dense) which increases fragmentation on the paged PT layout. that interacts badly with our async-evict path.

tara: repro steps? i can run a canary.

alex: quick repro: `./run_eval --model redwood-3b --longctx 64k --warmup 20 --iters 200 --profile kv`
Key lines from the profiler (trimmed):
```
KV_PAGER: evict_count=462, page_faults=312, pt_frag_index=0.74, cache_resident=0.62
KERNEL: selected tiled_small_v2 for batch=12, seq=256
TRACE: pt_walk_latency_p50=0.9ms p99=7.2ms
```

ci-bot: kvcache-integration (linux-h100) — run 7821 failed 3/5 tests. link: https://ci/redwood/7821#logs

morgan: i ran a trace on MI250x and saw a different symptom: mapping order gets reversed under concurrent remap which causes the reclaim loop to revisit recently freed slots (makes fragmentation look worse). trace snippet: `pt_shadow_unmap -> remap_insert -> reclaim_loop restart` — looks like an ordering/race in the pt remap code path.

sasha: so two separate but compounding issues: (1) kernel selection changes physical touch order which increases fragmentation pressure, (2) concurrent remap/reclaim ordering on some hw (mi250x) amplifies the churn.

sasha: short-term mitigation: revert `prefer_small_batch_kernels` or gate it behind a runtime flag that we default off for paged-attention models. also add a heuristic: only pick small-batch kernel when recent reuse_rate > 0.8 (prevents pathological warmup-phase evict storms).

alex: agreed. i'll put up a small runtime-flagged patch: `kv_pt_safe_mode` that forces legacy kernel selection and slightly raises batch_threshold back to 28 for paged-attn flows. will run canaries on h100/a100/mi250.

tara: can we also emit an eviction-age histogram? we lack visibility into reuse decay which would help tune the threshold.

alex: added to PR TODO. PR: https://git/redwood/pulls/4821 — includes: flag, metric:evict_age_histogram, and a temporary rollback of `prefer_small_batch_kernels` for paged-attn. will post perf diffs once canaries finish.

morgan: thanks — tagging eng-runtime-oncall to watch: @sasha @tara

sasha: quick note: if we keep small-batch kernels, we should also change their inner loop to do coalesced page touches (scan by page rather than by tile). i sketched a patch but want to validate perf.

alex: good point. i'll land the gate rollback first, then follow-up with the coalesced-touch patch behind a perf flag.

tara: :thumbsup: please add the canary links to the PR description and include the `--profile kv` snapshots for each GPU.

alex: will do. current plan: rollback gate now, run canaries, then iterate on kernel inner-loop change + reuse-aware batching. updates in this thread.
